newsitem.title: SPAIN: POLL-Bank of Spain seen leaving key rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Bank of Spain seen leaving key rate unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is expected to leave its 5.75 percent money market rate unchanged at its regular repurchase auction on Thursday, analysts said.
In a Reuter poll of eight analysts and dealers conducted on Wednesday, all ruled out a rate change.
"Money market rates are very stable. It seems nobody is expecting any change in the next three to four months," said a money market dealer in Madrid who was polled.
All analysts surveyed said there had been no change in the economic outlook since the central bank trimmed its key money rate by 25 basis points at the last auction on March 14.
Most of those polled agreed there is room for at least one more 25 basis point cut later this year, depending on the performance of inflation and peseta exchange rates.
Spain's February CPI eased to 2.5 percent year-on-year, from 2.9 percent the previous month.
Analysts agreed the international rate outlook had changed after the recent U.S. rate increase.
The Bank of Spain started its current cycle of rate reductions in December 1995, when it cut its official rate to nine percent from 9.25 percent.
